messages:
maria: Heads up — after the kernel-selector v2.5 roll we saw a cluster of CUDA OOMs on asia-prod-rt-2. GPUs hit sudden memory surge and several requests hard-failed. Root dump looks like KV cache growth + very large combined batch sizes. Attaching a short log excerpt. :fire:

maria: ```
[2026-03-18T10:01:23Z] cuda: out of memory (allocation 512MB)
[2026-03-18T10:01:23Z] runtime: workspace reserve 1.6GB -> failure
[2026-03-18T10:01:23Z] kvcache: entries=1.2M, total_kv_bytes=6.1GB
[2026-03-18T10:01:23Z] batcher: batching_window=200ms, combined_tokens=42000
```

kevin: oncall triage starting. @infra-bot kick perf traces + collect kernel/allocator metrics from the node pools. :eyes:

infra-bot: perf traces job started: https://perf.redwood/internal/jobs/9876
infra-bot: nodepool=asia-prod-rt-2, pods affected=7, average-latency-surge=2.3x

nathan: quick theory: kernel-selector v2.5 picked the 'fast-mem' kernel for long-context flows which uses larger per-workspace allocations. Combined with the auto-batcher merging many long chats we end up allocating huge workspaces + keeping big KV sets in memory. Two-pronged mitigation: force conservative kernel fallback + short-circuit big auto-batches.

maria: what are the immediate safe ops? canary rollback or runtime feature flip?

nathan: safe immediate steps (do in order):
1) flip kernel selector to conservative for asia-prod-rt-2
2) enable request-size circuit-breaker to reject requests where input_tokens + context_kv_tokens > 12k
3) temporarily set kvcache.max_entries=200k and eviction_policy=aggressive
4) set batcher.max_combined_tokens=8192 and batching_window=20ms
5) scale a few extra nodes as breathing room if commit windows allow

nathan: commands to run (use redwoodctl):
```bash
redwoodctl feature-flip set kernel_selector=conservative --scope nodepool=asia-prod-rt-2
redwoodctl config set cluster.asia-prod-rt-2.batch.max_combined_tokens=8192
redwoodctl config set cluster.asia-prod-rt-2.batch.window_ms=20
redwoodctl config set cluster.asia-prod-rt-2.kvcache.max_entries=200000
redwoodctl config set cluster.asia-prod-rt-2.kvcache.eviction=aggressive
```

ashley: I'm applying the kernel_selector flip now on the targeted nodepool. Will watch for failed request rate and GPU memory.

prod-oncall-bot: Change applied by ashley at 2026-03-18T10:04:12Z. Rolling to nodes (3/3 updated).

ashley: kernel selector reverted to conservative, batcher caps set. Initial glance: OOMs stopped immediately on the updated nodes. memory profiles trending down. :white_check_mark:

maria: great. can we confirm KV shrink? I'll run kvcache snapshot query.

ashley: kvcache snapshot (post-change): entries=185k, total_kv_bytes=880MB. Pre-change peaked at ~6.1GB.

kevin: confirm: reduced combined_tokens in batches from ~42k down to <6k within 30s of change. Means batching heuristics were the bigger multiplier. We should keep circuit-breaker for 1h and monitor.

nathan: follow-ups to add to postmortem / actions:
- add per-tenant KV growth alert (rate-of-change + absolute threshold)
- add kernel-selector canary gating tied to kvcache memory signals (abort rollout if sustained growth > 30% in 5m)
- tighten default batcher.max_combined_tokens for long-context models, and make auto-batcher prefer latency-preserving merges
- add an emergency `reject-if-kv-growth` circuit and a low-latency path that disables kvcache for offending requests

sara: note for playbook: include a one-click runbook in Console that atomically flips kernel_selector + batch caps + kvcache eviction. We lost time coordinating the separate changes.

maria: agree. also document the exact log signatures to look for (batcher.combined_tokens > 30k && kvcache.total_kv_bytes > 4GB) and wire an alert to #oncall-prod.

kevin: marking incident as mitigated for now — keeping monitoring on for 60m. Will open a postmortem ticket with timeline and metric graphs. :spiral_calendar_pad:

sara: adding retro items to product backlog: conservative canary threshold, operator one-click mitigation, and a simulation test that replays long-chat traffic through kernel-selector.

maria: thanks team. good job moving fast. closing thread once postmortem ticket is created. :tada:
